To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a CTL harvesting system with a feller bunch and two processors working in combination is more productive than a single harvester-processor, but its use is not cost effective in areas with moderately to steep slopes and small tree diameter.

the use of a cut-to-length harvesting system with a feller bunching attachment is more productive than a single-grip harvester-processor in moderately steep terrain, but its use is not cost effective in areas with steep terrain and small diameter trees.

1) the use of a CTL harvester in conjunction with two processors is the most productive and cost-effective harvesting system for thinning operations in native forest regrowth with small tree size and steep terrain; 2) the use of two processors working in tandem is a cost-effective harvesting system when the tree diameter is large and the terrain is moderately steep; and 3) the use of harvester-processor is the most cost-effective harvesting system in areas with small tree diameter and gentle terrain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic feasibility of using a feller bunching machine working in conjunction with a cut-to-length harvesting system in the Australian native forest environment.
the evaluation of alternative CTL harvesting technology for native forest thinning in Australia.

the evaluation of the productivity of two harvesting systems (harvester-processor and feller buncher and processors) in native forest re-generation thinning in the context of the Australian environment, where the use of the CTL harvesting system has not been common practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a single-grip harvester working alone in a cut-to-length system is more productive, more cost-effective, and more environmentally sound than the combination of a feller-buncher and two processors in the areas and conditions studied.
the use of a single-grip harvester is recommended for areas with moderately steep and gentle slope terrain and average tree diameters of 20 to 25 cm.
a single-grip harvester working alone is more cost efficient than the use of two machines in a CTL system for the harvesting of small diameter trees in moderately steep terrain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a single harvester-processor in combination with a forwarder is the most productive and cost-effective system for the harvesting of small trees (diameter less than 20 cm).
a harvester- processor is more cost effective than a feller bunching system in most cases.
, for the range of terrain conditions and tree diameters evaluated, the use of a single-grip harvester-processor was more productive than the feller buncher and processors system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the productivity of a CTL harvesting system is highly influenced by tree diameter, and therefore the cost of the harvesting system is highly dependent on tree diameter.

in the Australian native forest thinning environment the use of a CTL harvesting system with a harvester- processor working alone is more economical than a CTL harvesting system using a feller bunching machine in combination with two processing machines.
the cost of harvesting operations is highly influenced by tree size and the terrain.
